blocks.text: Database constraints enforce order integrity even when writes bypass the API.
TYPE NOT NULL rejects nulls independently of the application path.

UNIQUE rejects duplicate combinations; PostgreSQL treats nulls as distinct by default unless NULLS NOT DISTINCT is specified. PRIMARY KEY gives unique non-null row identity and may span columns. FOREIGN KEY requires non-null references to match referenced rows. CHECK constrains row values but passes on true or null; add NOT NULL to reject absence.

blocks.code:
CREATE TABLE orders (
    identity INTEGER,
    customer_reference INTEGER,
    quantity INTEGER NOT NULL,
    external_reference TEXT,
    PRIMARY KEY (identity),
    FOREIGN KEY (customer_reference) REFERENCES customers (identity),
    CHECK (quantity > 0),
    UNIQUE (external_reference)
);

annotations.text: customers already exists with identity as its primary key. PRIMARY KEY may list multiple columns. CHECK passes on true or null, so quantity also needs NOT NULL. UNIQUE preserves PostgreSQL’s default distinct-null behavior; UNIQUE NULLS NOT DISTINCT (external_reference) is the alternative when null duplicates must also be rejected.

blocks.text: Inspect proposed orders independently against the baseline. PRIMARY KEY protects unique non-null identity, and FOREIGN KEY checks non-null customer references. quantity needs NOT NULL as well as CHECK. UNIQUE rejects duplicate external references, but PostgreSQL’s default permits distinct nulls; NULLS NOT DISTINCT changes that null comparison. Match each violation to its constraint.
CHECK passing on null does not replace NOT NULL. PostgreSQL UNIQUE treats nulls as distinct by default.

blocks.text: Database constraints enforce integrity beyond the API. CHECK does not reject null by itself; default UNIQUE treats nulls as distinct.
Declare UNIQUE (columns) to reject duplicate combinations; PostgreSQL treats nulls as distinct by default unless NULLS NOT DISTINCT is specified.
Contrast CHECK (quantity > 0) alone with adding NOT NULL: null passes CHECK alone but is rejected by NOT NULL.
Declare a column as TYPE NOT NULL to reject nulls independently of whether a write came through an application.
Declare CHECK (condition) to constrain values in a row; a check passes when its expression is true or null, so use NOT NULL separately when absence must be rejected.
Contrast CHECK (quantity > 0) alone with adding NOT NULL: null passes CHECK alone but is rejected by NOT NULL.
Declare a column as TYPE NOT NULL to reject nulls independently of whether a write came through an application.
Declare PRIMARY KEY (columns) for unique non-null row identity; a primary key can contain more than one column.
Declare FOREIGN KEY (columns) REFERENCES target (columns) so non-null referencing values must match referenced rows.
Contrast CHECK (quantity > 0) alone with adding NOT NULL: null passes CHECK alone but is rejected by NOT NULL.

For external_reference, add UNIQUE (external_reference) inside the table declaration. This rejects a repeated non-null value such as ORD-A. Keep external_reference nullable and use the default UNIQUE policy: repeated null external references are permitted. Do not add NULLS NOT DISTINCT in this exercise, because it changes that requested null policy. Each proposed row is checked independently against the supplied baseline.
